to Stay
slides.subtitle: A rights-aware, evidence-audited framework for connected hospitality experiences.
slides.body: Working proposition: the in-room display can be treated as an orchestration layer connecting guest-facing capabilities, operational systems, and property-specific value questions.
slides.alt_text: HXG title slide presents a working proposition and previews six capability-to-outcome pathways.

slides.title: A smaller evidence set. A stronger audit trail.
slides.subtitle: HXG v0.3.0 removes restricted statistics, commercial-research claims, and vendor evidence edges.
slides.scope: Original HXG analysis plus reviewed open-license and public-information sources. Every public source has a current machine-readable rights record.
slides.body: The pathways are analytical propositions for evaluation - not empirical guest preferences, causal findings, or universal product claims.
slides.alt_text: Six experience pathways, three evidence states, and one auditable framework, with an analytical-not-empirical caveat.

slides.title: Six capabilities. Six questions to validate.
slides.body: Each one-to-one pathway uses the bounded verb can support. The relationship IDs resolve to original HXG analytical claims and explicit limitations.
slides.alt_text: Six rows connect guest-facing capabilities to six guest outcomes using the bounded phrase can support.

slides.title: Use formulas to expose assumptions - not to imply ROI.

formulae.heading: Ancillary contribution
formulae.body: Eligible occupied room nights x measured engagement x incremental conversion x contribution margin.

formulae.heading: Energy value
formulae.body: Verified baseline x controllable share x measured attributable reduction.

formulae.heading: Operational support
formulae.body: Verified remote resolutions x measured avoided dispatch cost.

slides.context: No universal rate, uplift, saving, conversion, or ROI is supplied. Every input, counterfactual, and attribution decision belongs to the property.
slides.alt_text: Three variable-based value formulas for ancillary contribution, energy, and operational support, all requiring local measurement.

slides.title: Every stakeholder owns a different proof burden.
slides.context: HXG maps questions and responsibilities. It does not assign revenue, savings, or guest outcomes to a stakeholder without local evidence.
slides.alt_text: Stakeholders are grouped by who experiences, operates, enables, and validates value.

slides.title: Samsung Hospitality - links, not evidence.
slides.disclosure: Samsung is referenced descriptively through publicly available product links. HXG is independent and is not sponsored, endorsed, reviewed, or approved by Samsung.
slides.alt_text: Four metadata-only Samsung product links appear beside a clear independence disclosure; none is used as evidence.

slides.title: Confidence includes permission to use the source.

states.name: Direct fact
states.example: A paraphrased statement from a reviewed open source.

states.name: Supported inference
states.example: An HXG proposition linked to evidence and limitations.

states.name: Modeled scenario
states.example: A transparent formula awaiting property inputs.

contradictions: Analytical pathway is not preference evidence
Security controls do not guarantee perception
slides.limitations: Unknown, denied, missing, or expired rights fail closed before retrieval. Vendor links stay outside cache, model context, claims, and graph relationships.
slides.alt_text: Three evidence states, four major limitations, and the fail-closed source-rights policy.

slides.title: Audit the chain. Challenge the framework.
slides.body: Release 0.3.0 is a deterministic rights-policy rebuild with disclosed human governance. Models did not run. Python owns validation, counts, graph exports, and publication files.
slides.alt_text: Eight rights-aware research stages, generated release counts, the live HXG URL, QR code, and an invitation to audit the framework.
